note:
Malcolm, 2026-08-25: the f3 block on /pages/copper-peptide-research — 'Greater satisfaction with skin appearance (independent trial)' — should carry a SKIN MODEL PHOTOGRAPH, not another medical explainer: a facial close-up of a beautiful smiling 35-year-old woman gently touching the skin on her cheek. Batch requested.

WHY A PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT HERE, AND ONLY HERE. The three key-findings blocks are not the same kind of claim. f1 (Pickart 2018) and f2 (Kang 2009) are measured biology — collagen synthesis, basal-cell markers in a skin-equivalent model — so they get cross-section explainers. f3 (Miller 2006) is SELF-REPORTED SATISFACTION over 12 weeks: what changed is how the user felt about their skin. A person appraising her own face with pleasure is a literal depiction of that endpoint, where a third explainer would illustrate a mechanism the study never measured. The register change from illustration to photograph is the point, not a lapse.

WHAT THE FRAME MUST NOT IMPLY. Self-reported means self-reported. No before/after, no split, no comparison of any kind, no measurement overlay, no clinical setting, no lab coat, no white-room medical staging — those all read as an objective result and this study has none. Just a woman who likes her skin. The alt text at publish time must not describe her as a trial participant either.

BOX GEOMETRY — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Live DOM at 390 / 1024 / 1440: the media box is 1:1 at EVERY width (350x350 mobile, 660x660 desktop, capped 720), object-fit cover, object-position 50% 50%. So a square master is delivered whole and nothing is cropped. Note this CONTRADICTS the composition note in page-copper-peptide-research-key-finding-2.json, which claimed the box is taller than wide and crops top and bottom; that was wrong and no square has ever been cropped here. Generate 2048x2048.

HANDEDNESS. At 1440 the section alternates media_position: f1 image-left, f2 image-right, f3 IMAGE-LEFT with the text to its right. So her turn and gaze should favour frame-right on most variants — leaning into the copy rather than away from it. One variant looks straight down the lens, which is handedness-neutral.

THE ONE THING THAT WILL DECIDE THIS BATCH IS SKIN, AND IT IS AN ENGINE PROBLEM. On 2026-08-24 Malcolm rejected the PDRN hero on skin quality alone: 'you can see its not natural enough (AI detail distortions). Its subtle - but isnt quite good enough.' Zoomed to native pixels, the artefact was a swirling fingerprint-like whorl of concentric wavy micro-lines on the cheek beside the eye, present in nbp_flash, nbp_pro AND seedream, and ABSENT from gpt-image. This brief is nothing but cheek beside eye at close range, so that comparison is the whole ballgame: gpt-image is expected to win, and every supplier still runs per rule 1. The skin_clause below names the specific artefact rather than vaguely asking for realism, and describes what real skin does — per the 'the brief caused the plainness' lesson, it forbids the machine pattern, never texture itself.

AGE IS SPECIFIED BY EVIDENCE, NOT BY NUMBER. These engines read 'thirty-five' and render twenty-two. Each brief therefore names the physical markers of thirty-five — fine lines at the outer eye corners that deepen into real creases when she smiles, a faint line across the forehead, a little softness at the jaw — so the age arrives as anatomy rather than as a word. Per 'describe the thing, don't name it'.

HANDS AND TEETH ARE THE TWO FAILURE SURFACES. Every brief states exactly how many fingers are visible, which ones, where each makes contact, and that the fingertips dimple the skin slightly so the touch is a real one under real weight rather than a hand hovering in front of a face. Two variants smile with teeth and two smile closed-lipped, deliberately, so a batch-wide dental failure still leaves usable frames.

CLASS B THROUGHOUT — no product in frame, no references attached, therefore no product description and no brand identity given to any engine ('reference-free shots must not get product desc'). FLUX.2 is in the run: there is no branding for it to invent, and it is good on skin studies.

GROUNDS follow the palette. A/B/D sit on Bone F0F0F0 and Pearl grey D8D6D4, keeping the block bright beside the two high-key explainers above it. C is on Clinical blue 014EB1, this page's own ingredient colour, offered as the on-brand option — it will read as a bolder, more campaign-like frame and is flagged as such rather than assumed.

defaults.skin_clause: Skin rendered as a real unretouched photograph at high resolution: pores of visibly varying size and irregular spacing, fine lines running in the natural directions of the face, a few genuine freckles and one or two small moles placed irregularly, soft vellus hair catching the light along the temple and jaw, and uneven sheen so some areas read matte and others slightly shiny. No allover pattern of any kind: the texture must never resolve into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or a repeating weave anywhere, and least of all on the cheek beside the eye. Mature, assured, in her middle thirties, not a woman in her twenties.

slots.title: A · open warm smile, three fingertips flat on the cheekbone, turned to frame right
slots.prompt:
High-end beauty campaign photograph, square format, a close-up of the face of a beautiful Caucasian woman in her middle thirties, a professional beauty campaign model with fine even features, clear grey-green eyes and softly waved light brown hair pushed back from her face. The crop is close: her face fills most of the frame, the top of her head is cut by the upper edge and her chin sits a little above the lower edge. Her head and shoulders are turned about thirty degrees toward the right side of the frame while her eyes come back to the camera, and she is smiling a wide genuine smile with her lips parted, even natural teeth showing, the smile reaching her eyes and gathering the skin at their outer corners.

Her right hand is raised to her face. Three fingers only are visible - index, middle and ring - held loosely together and relaxed, their pads lying flat against the round of her cheekbone just below the outer corner of her eye, the thumb tucked out of sight below the jaw and the little finger curled away. The fingertips press lightly enough to dimple the skin very slightly where they rest, so the touch carries real weight instead of hovering. The fingers are slender, the nails short, bare and unpainted. The hand is unhurried and affectionate, appraising her own skin with pleasure.

SHE IS THIRTY-FIVE AND READS AS THIRTY-FIVE: fine lines at the outer corners of both eyes that gather into real creases as she smiles, a faint horizontal line across the forehead, the very beginning of a soft line from nose to mouth corner, and a jaw that is defined but no longer knife-sharp. Mature, assured, in her middle thirties, not a woman in her twenties.

SKIN RENDERED AS A REAL UNRETOUCHED PHOTOGRAPH at high resolution: pores of visibly varying size and irregular spacing, fine lines running in the natural directions of the face, a few genuine freckles and one or two small moles placed irregularly, soft vellus hair catching the light along the temple and jaw, and uneven sheen so some areas read matte and others slightly shiny. No allover pattern of any kind: the texture must never resolve into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or a repeating weave anywhere, and least of all on the cheek beside the eye. Skin healthy and luminous but unmistakably real, never airbrushed to plastic.

Makeup barely there: skin left as skin, brows groomed but natural, a softly tinted lip in a warm nude, no visible base or powder. Behind her a seamless pale off-white backdrop, colour hex F0F0F0, thrown well out of focus. A broad soft key light from the front and slightly above with a gentle fill from below, giving one clean catchlight in each eye and a soft real shadow under the jaw. 100mm lens at f4, natural skin tones, clean neutral grade, editorial beauty advertising quality.
slots.negative_extra: chin resting on the hand, hand covering the mouth, hand across the eyes, fingers spread wide, palm flat against the cheek, two hands

slots.title: B · very tight near-profile, eyes closed, closed-lip smile, backs of the fingers grazing the cheek
slots.prompt:

Serene, pleased, self-possessed.

Her hand comes up to the far side of her face. Only the backs of the index and middle fingers are visible, curled loosely inward, grazing the skin of her cheek just beneath the cheekbone and drawing very lightly along it, the knuckles rounded and relaxed and the remaining fingers folded down out of sight. No allover pattern of any kind: the texture must never resolve into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or a repeating weave anywhere, and least of all on the cheek beside the eye.
